gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-sono: Sono is a sans with wide default spacing and a lowercase a that leaves its mouth ajar. But Plakkaat does the loud work, heavy bent-straw strokes with terminals curling nearly shut, while Sono keeps everything open.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-tiktok-sans: Plakkaat draws every stroke with a neon-tube consistency, heavy and bent like straw, its terminals curling almost back to the stem. TikTok Sans opens up beside it, its x-height nearly matching the caps.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-vend-sans: Vend Sans holds a ruler-straight line, its curves ending in wide, unclosed terminals. Plakkaat hits harder with its closed, bent-straw heaviness, while Vend Sans does its best work filling the line with a generous x-height.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-aldrich: Aldrich reads like tracing one thick thread, its round letters cupped rather than clenched, its x-height close to the caps. And Quantum's loose letterfit and open mouths supply the spaciousness that makes the pair feel clean and techy.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-alexandria: Quantum has a pen-plotter smoothness and loose letterfit with lots of breathing space. Quantum does its best with a few spacious display words, while the sans-serif Alexandria offers broad c terminals and short stems above and below.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-amiko: Loose and techy: Quantum lets its letters breathe, with mouths open and ascenders kept short. Amiko brings crayon-thick lowercase strokes and tong-like terminals, and that sturdy-versus-loose pull is what makes the pair work.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-anek-devanagari: Anek Devanagari is a modern sans with distinctly open letter mouths. As text runs on, its large middle zone keeps lines unhurried and legible, while Quantum stays smooth and swell-free up in the headings.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-anek-gurmukhi: Quantum keeps its letters loose, mouths open and ascenders compressed. Anek Gurmukhi, the sans-serif below, carries open-handed curves and generous counters, so a shared openness runs through the whole pair.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-anek-kannada: Quantum gives each stroke the same visual weight, loose and smooth. Anek Kannada brings a high, squared-off x-height and terminals that stop far from the stem, so running text should feel open and brisk.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-anek-latin: Quantum draws like ruler and compass, smooth and loose, with ascenders cut short. Anek Latin is a sans with lowercase nearly reaching the capitals, and if Quantum is made small, its breathing space starts to scatter.
